$$\begin{aligned}6-x&=0\\x&=6\end{aligned}$$

The function is undefined at these values. Desmos confirms vertical asymptotes at $x=2,3$.

entries.description: Piecewise-Defined Function

Piecewise-Defined Function
• A piecewise function combines more than one function in different parts of its domain.
f(x) = { g(x), x ≤ a; h(x), x > a }.
• f(x) is called the piecewise-defined function.
• g(x) and h(x) are called subfunctions.
• To sketch a piecewise-defined function:
1. Identify the graphs of each subfunction and their domains.
2. Calculate function values at the boundaries.
3. Sketch each subfunction separately.
Decide whether to connect the curves or use open/closed circles.

entries.description:
A function is discontinuous at x = a if:
• The function is undefined at that point (e.g. asymptote, denominator = 0).
• A piecewise function doesn’t join up at x = a.

Given a piecewise function:
f(x) = { g(x), x ≤ a; h(x), x > a }
The function is continuous at x = a if g(a) = h(a).
The function is discontinuous at x = a if g(a) ≠ h(a).

We will assume the curve is continuous everywhere else.
